Hi Evelyn,

Quick intro: Aperture is scheduling a 12-week pilot (internal triage assistant) that will touch PHI and must remain logically isolated from other customers. We have two procurement lanes we want you to cost out for the pilot and a potential production rollout: (1) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity owned by Redwood for our tenant) and (2) Private (VPC/private control plane deployed into our cloud account).

Key constraints:
- Data classification: PHI (must be encrypted at rest and in transit; SOC2 + evidence required)
- No air-gapped requirement, but VPC peering + customer-managed KMS preferred for Private option
- Target tail latency: <= 350ms 95th for single-step chat completions
- Pilot expected peak: approx 45-60 requests/sec; median prompt tokens ~120; max sequence length ~1024 tokens
- Burst tolerance: up to 3x sustained spikes for short periods (10-20 minutes)

Can you provide a short comparison (sizing + monthly cost ballpark + fallback ladder for burst events) and an operational runbook for the pilot? We also need a list of artifacts you’ll need for procurement (SOC2 scope, encryption notes, PO flow). I attached a short requirements doc.

Thanks — can we get a first pass by EOD tomorrow? Procurement is on a tight cadence.

Samira

Hi Samira — follow-up with a concise comparison and a recommended pilot slate. I summarized assumptions based on your CSV and our defaults. Please treat the numbers as a first pass; we'll refine once we validate model selection and exact QPS windows.

Summary (assumptions): avg request tokens = 120; median latency target 95p <= 350ms; model: 33B quantized (8-bit) for baseline, 70B q4f16 as accuracy uplift test for 10% of traffic. Peak sustained pilot: 60 RPS. KV cache hit rate assumed 30% for multi-turn chat.

Option A — Dedicated (Reserved Redwood capacity)
- Suggested footprint for pilot: 8 x A100-80GB equiv (or 10 x A40 equiv) in a dedicated pool.
- Why: predictable throughput, single-tenant scheduling reduces noisy neighbor risk, simpler SLA for tail latency.
- Benefits: Redwood handles management and burst into reserved pool.
- Weakness: higher monthly commit cost; requires reserved contract for pilot months to secure capacity.
- Monthly ballpark: $65k–$85k (in-region US pricing, includes baseline reserved + monitoring/observability add-on).

Option B — Private (VPC / customer-controlled infra)
- Suggested footprint for pilot: 4–6 nodes of A100-80GB equiv (depending on VM sizing) deployed in your VPC plus a small Redwood-hosted burst lane (2 nodes) for overflow via encrypted egress.
- Why: customer control of KMS and network boundaries, easier to satisfy some procurement/security checkboxes.
- Benefits: aligns with customer-managed keys and audit controls; lower Redwood-managed monthly fees but higher cloud infra ops for Aperture.
- Weakness: onboarding/setup time longer, engineering ops owned by Aperture, burst behavior needs explicit stitching plan to Redwood-run nodes which adds complexity.
- Monthly ballpark (infra + maintenance): $40k–$55k + estimated 15% operations uplift.

Hybrid pattern (recommended for pilot): Start Private with 4 nodes + Redwood-managed burst stitching. If pilot crosses a growth threshold (3x sustained for 48h), convert to Dedicated reserved pool to stabilize tail latency.

Operational notes:
- Stitching approach: keep model weights and KV cache local; route overflow traffic to a quantized compatible variant on Redwood-hosted nodes. All transit uses mTLS and per-tenant encryption.
- Fallback ladder: 1) local VPC cache warming; 2) Redwood burst (quantized model variant) with degraded accuracy flagging to clients; 3) shed non-critical batch workloads; 4) temporary rate limits per-session.
- Audit artifacts we'll provide: SOC2 summary, KMS integration checklist, network peering diagram, and sample runbook.

Next steps: I'll convert this into a 1-page executive summary and a short technical appendix; expect a PDF by tomorrow morning. Evelyn — can you confirm the procurement checklist items we need to pre-fill?

- Marissa

Thanks — a couple of technical clarifications and a quick schematic attached.

A few engineering notes:
- Stitching schematic: we propose a light tenant-proxy in your VPC that does request routing and local KV cache. Overflow is proxied over an encrypted tunnel to Redwood burst nodes. This keeps PHI out of Redwood storage (we only accept ephemeral encrypted payloads for burst handling). See attached gpu_stitching_schematic.png.
- Sizing rationale: 33B quantized at 8-bit typically requires ~18–22GB GPU RAM active per instance for reasonable batch/latency tradeoffs. For 60 RPS with 95p <=350ms, 8 A100-80GB equiv gives comfortable headroom with batching and KV cache.
- Isolation controls: we can support customer-managed KMS for keys and will surface audit logs (S3-compatible signed logs) to your audit account. SOC2 evidence: we can provide the SOC2 bridge letter + redacted control matrices.
- Canary/fallback policy: route 10% of traffic to quantized variant in Redwood for 48h; if latency and quality metrics are acceptable, increase to 25% then full cutover.

I'll hand this schematic and the brief runbook to our ops team to prep any network templates needed for VPC peering.

- Karthik
